To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AMDF, SIFT, and parallel processing methods are the best of the seven methods for telephone recordings.

(1) the cepstral pitch detector is the best pitch detector for the telephone condition; (2) the AMDF pitch detector is best for the wideband condition; (3) the cepstral and the SIFT detectors are the best for the close-talking condition; (4) the AMDF detector is the best for high pitched speech; (5) the cepstral detector is the best detector for low pitched speech.
the cepstral method is best for telephone recordings and the SIFT method is best for close-talking recordings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the performance of several pitch detection algorithms as a function of the type of speech data, recording condition, and the pitch of the speaker.
the development of a pitch detection algorithm which is capable of operating in the presence of a wide variety of background noise, reverberation, pitch range, and pitch contour characteristics.
the development and evaluation of pitch detectors which can be used to provide accurate pitch contours for use in speech research and in speech processing applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SIFT algorithm performed best for telephone recordings, the cepstral method performed best for close-talking microphones, and the spectral flattening LPC algorithm performed best for wideband recordings.
no single pitch detector is best under all conditions.
the cepstral method is best for the telephone condition, the parallel processing time-domain method is best for close talking microphone condition, and the AMDF method is best for wideband condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AMDF method was the most accurate pitch detector, and the SIFT method was the most robust.

all of the algorithms tested performed well on the close talking microphone data, but that the performance of each algorithm varied widely as a function of the pitch range of the speaker and the recording condition.
the AMDF algorithm is the most accurate pitch detector for the data base used in this study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMDF method was the most reliable pitch detector for the wideband recordings and for the close-talking recordings.
no one pitch detection algorithm is superior to the others.
the AMDF method performed best for the data set used in this study.
